Burham said he wanted a "dialogue with those affected by the slave trade" and was open to "calls for an apology". He dismissed the idea of paying financial reparations, saying they were "not the right answer". The comments come ahead of a Commonwealth leaders summit in the Caribbean next week, which Burnham will attend. Caribbean nations have renewed calls for the UK to apologise for its role in the slave trade, and for reparations, as King Charles III tours the region . Burham described the transatlantic slave trade, when Africans were trafficked to the Americas, as a "brutal and barbaric violation" and said Britain must "face up to the past". The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations. Burnham has stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and has stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments. "I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part," Burnham wrote in his piece for the Guardian , external . He said Commonwealth countries had for years been asking for an "honest conversation". Burnham said he wanted to offer a "structured dialogue" adding: "Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process. clusters.text: In a memo shared with Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers this week, and later obtained by MacRumors , Apple provided technicians with guidance on how to diagnose and address the iPhone Duo's inner display cracking issue. If a customer reports the issue, Apple advised technicians to inspect the iPhone Duo and repair or replace it in accordance with their standard procedures. While the instructions themselves are straightforward, the fact that Apple issued an internal memo suggests the issue is widespread enough to warrant official guidance. Apple's memo said the issue affects a small number of iPhone Duo units, which is consistent with what it said in a public statement on Monday. "We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units," said Apple, in a statement shared with MacRumors . If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement." You can get support on Apple's website or by calling 1-800-APL-CARE in the U.S. and Canada. Apple said most iPhone Duo units are not susceptible to this issue and that impacted units appear to exhibit the defects rather quickly after usage. Apple said there is no iPhone Duo recall, and the company has yet to launch a public-facing repair program on its website for this issue. Almost immediately after the iPhone Duo began arriving to customers a week ago, a handful of early adopters reported that the device's inner display had cracked , resulting in lines appearing down the middle and towards the right side of the screen. The electronics repair website iFixit completed an iPhone Duo teardown and said that the issue is likely related to a defective hinge on affected units. However, Apple has yet to comment on the underlying cause of the issue.

clusters.text: A meteorite found in the Sahara is a rare piece of Mars’ ancient crust. Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one. A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It’s very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says. “We don’t fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth,” Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars’ gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Exxon's energy products business earned $9.05 billion in adjusted profit, up from $4.1 billion in the second quarter. Its U.S. Gulf Coast refinery units operated at 100% utilization, producing their second-highest diesel volumes on record. clusters.text: Ranchi, Oct 31 (PTI) Three members of a family were arrested for allegedly killing a 38-year-old revenue department official at his house in Ranchi after he rejected mutation of a land parcel due to discrepancies in documents, police said on Saturday. also: Salesforce reportedly agrees to buy defense tech startup Rune for $375 million
clusters.text: Salesforce has agreed to acquire startup Rune Technologies for $375 million in cash and stock. Rune develops artificial intelligence-based software that helps the U.S. military forecast supply needs and manage logistics in field conditions. Resilience Media reported the deal, TechCrunch writes. The deal is expected to strengthen Missionforce, a Salesforce unit that works with national security agencies and defense departments. In its blog, Salesforce said that since Missionforce launched last year, its business has grown by 80% year over year. This was partly driven by a new 10-year, $5.6 billion contract with the U.S. Army. Salesforce plans to integrate Rune’s frontline logistics data into Missionforce. This is expected to expand the unit’s capabilities from administrative planning in the rear to supporting operations on the battlefield. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Rune Technologies was founded in 2024. Since then, the startup has raised a total of $30 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Point72 Ventures, and IQT, a nonprofit venture company backed by the CIA and formerly known as In-Q-Tel. According to PitchBook, Rune was valued at $127 million during its Series A round, which was led by Human Capital last year. This year, Salesforce also agreed to acquire the AI agent platform Fin, formerly known as Intercom, for $3.6 billion, bought Qualified for $1.2 billion, and reached a deal to acquire Listen Labs. Salesforce did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

clusters.title: Chaos at Prayagraj Run for Unity marathon: 5,000-6,000 people protest, break chairs and snatch certificates...
clusters.text: A commotion broke out during the Run for Unity marathon held in Prayagraj on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary. Around 6,000 students took part in the event. The trouble started when the race began soon after registration without explaining the rules or holding a formal flag-off. This led to confusion among the participants, and chairs were broken during the chaos. The marathon was organised by the BJP's Yamunapar unit. Around 5,000 people took part in the 5-km race held in Naini. The BJP's Prayagraj Yamunapar unit is organising a 5-km marathon in Naini on the occasion of National Unity Day. The race will start at 7 am from Abhinandan Guest House in Mewalal ki Bagiya and end at the selfie point near Sachcha Baba Ashram. BJP district vice-president Prof. Dr Devi Singh Patel is coordinating the event. According to the organisers, around 5,000 people are expected to take part in the marathon. Participants, public representatives and people working for public welfare, including those involved in de-addiction work, will also be honoured during the event. The winner will receive a prize of ₹11,000, while the runner-up will get ₹7,000. Meanwhile, a grand statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, also known as the Iron Man of India, installed by the Prayagraj Municipal Corporation on Sardar Patel Marg, will be unveiled on October 31. State Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh will unveil the statue at 1:30 pm. Preparations are under way for both events. Public representatives, BJP office-bearers, party workers, young people, sportspersons, prominent citizens and journalists have been invited to the National Unity Day programmes.

clusters.text: Prayagraj, Oct 31 (HS): Organized under the aegis of Madhubala Films and in collaboration with Rotary Prayagraj Sangam, the three-day International Prayagraj Film Festival 2026 was inaugurated with great pomp on Friday at Hotel Prayag Inn, Ashok Nagar, Prayagraj. Former Justice Sudhir Narayan Agarwal (Former Judge, Allahabad High Court) was present as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony. The program was presided over by Prof. Yogendra Pratap Singh, Director of Govind Ballabh Pant Social Science Institute, Prayagraj. Dr. Satpal Gulati, MD of United Group of Institutions and Dr. Shamsher Jamdagni, Additional Commissioner of Prayagraj were present as special guests. Guests at the ceremony praised the film festival, noting that cinema is not only a medium of entertainment, but also a powerful platform for expressing society, culture, literature, sensibilities, and ideas. Such events play a vital role in providing opportunities for new talent and in bringing Indian culture and creativity to national and international recognition. Chief Guest Justice Sudhir Narayan Agarwal praised the event, saying that it was a matter of pride to host an international film festival in a city like Prayagraj, which has a rich cultural and literary heritage. Congratulating the organizers, he said that such events strengthen the dialogue between art, culture, and society. Presiding over the event, Prof. Yogendra Pratap Singh said that cinema, besides being a reflection of society, is an effective medium for social change and positive thinking. Events like this in Prayagraj will serve to connect the rich tradition of literature, art, and culture with the new generation. Guest of Honor Dr. Satpal Gulati praised Madhubala Films' initiative, stating that the film festival is an important opportunity to provide a platform for creative talent and connect people associated with the film industry. He pledged his support for the event in the future. Guest of Honor Dr. Shamsher Jamdagni stated that Prayagraj has long been recognized as a city of education, literature, and culture. The International Film Festival will add a new dimension to this reputation. He extended his best wishes to the organizing committee and assured them of all possible support in the future.
